result: In a Norwegian nationwide registry of children (1,670 CFS/ME vs 4,937 T1DM and 1.34M general population), infectious mononucleosis was coded in the 2 years before diagnosis in 11.1% of CFS/ME vs 0.5% of T1DM, and infections overall were more common.
reason: Independent registry, paediatric, shows prior EBV/IM enrichment but does not test the viral-vs-bacterial contrast that the finding claims; extends rather than replicates.

result: In 89 women with CFS vs 26 matched controls, global grey matter volume did not differ; within patients, more pain (not fatigue) predicted lower left DLPFC grey matter volume and NAA/Cr.
reason: Independent structural MRI cohort with a null group difference in GMV, matching the finding's claim of no consistent volumetric abnormality.

result: In samples from the phase II rituximab trials, baseline serum BAFF was raised in 70 ME/CFS vs 56 controls (p=0.011), APRIL and T/NK subsets were unchanged by rituximab or response, and responders had lower baseline IgG (p=0.03).
reason: Mechanistic follow-up of the rituximab trials (B-cell effects not mediated through T/NK subsets); adds mechanism, no efficacy outcome.

result: In 60 CFS patients and 20 controls randomised to 15 min passive straight leg raise vs sham, true strain increased body pain (P=0.04), concentration difficulty (P=0.02) and composite symptoms during the manoeuvre, and lightheadedness (P=0.001) and composite score (P=0.005) at 24 h.
reason: Covered by the newer muscle-exertion-neuromuscular-strain finding; this may be its source study, so check for already cited.

result: Preliminary flow cytometry study found reduced TRPM3 surface expression on CD19+ B cells and CD56bright NK cells (17.4% vs 35.7%) in CFS/ME, with reduced cytoplasmic calcium after stimulation in B cells and CD56bright NK cells.
reason: Same research group as the finding's studies, so not an independent replication; adds surface expression and B cells to the NK calcium-influx finding.

result: In 120 adolescents with CFS vs 68 controls (NorCAPITAL), urine cortisol/creatinine ratio was lower and plasma norepinephrine, epinephrine and FT4 were higher, robust to case definition and confounder adjustment.
reason: Independent adolescent cohort with lower urinary cortisol, the same direction as the finding; the raised plasma catecholamines also bear on neuro-plasma-adrenaline.

result: In 15 CFS vs 10 controls scanned 6 years apart at 1.5 T, voxel-based morphometry showed a progressive decrease in white matter volume in the left inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus in CFS only.
reason: T1 volumetric VBM, not diffusion MRI; the volumetric content is covered by the neuro-mri-structure link.
